headline: An Iranian analyst says the stalemate is deliberate to influence the Nov 3 US midterms. Separately HT reports Don Jr. breaking
dek: Tehran's establishment expects renewed strikes, not talks; is deliberately prolonging the Hormuz deadlock to influence US midterms; Don Jr. publicly breaks with Trump on the war.
sources: Reuters (via HT relay); three anonymous Iranian sources; HT original on Don Jr.
fault_line: Is Iran refusing the deal out of strength — or gambling that a wider war won't come before November 3?

sections.what_happened: Tehran's establishment expects renewed strikes, not talks; is deliberately prolonging the Hormuz deadlock to influence US midterms; Don Jr. publicly breaks with Trump on the war.
sections.what_verified: Reuters attribution discipline (anonymous officials); consistent with earlier windows' deadlock reporting; Don Jr. element is HT original (not cross-checked).
sections.what_disputed: Iranian official statements (Baghaei) say retaliation posture, not deliberate election interference; anonymous sourcing cannot be independently verified.
sections.why_matters: Reuters' sources inside Tehran: Iran is preparing for new US-Israeli strikes, not a deal — and may be running the Hormuz clock to influence America's midterms. Meanwhile Don Jr. is breaking with his father on the war.
sections.context: Background: US-Iran — Hindustan Times relay of Reuters reporting: three Iranian sources (two officials + insider) say Tehran believes the US/Israel will launch another strike rather than engage in peace talks; 'Iran is preparing for renewed Israeli and US attacks, not for a deal'; an Iranian analyst says the stalemate is deliberate to influence the Nov 3 US midterms. Separately HT reports Don Jr. breaking with POTUS over the Iran war's electoral toll on Republicans.

totw_analysis: Our read: Reuters' sources inside Tehran: Iran is preparing for new US-Israeli strikes, not a deal — and may be running the Hormuz clock to influence America's midterms. Meanwhile Don Jr. is breaking with his father on the war. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Iran refusing the deal out of strength — or gambling that a wider war won't come before November 3?
related_short_title: Stalling on Purpose — Why Iran Wants the Talks to Drag Past November 3
